partners.mechanism_chain: NF1 (HGNC:7770) —DECREASES→ Ras signaling pathway (WP:WP44); Ras signaling pathway (WP:WP44) —LEADS_TO→ Cafe-au-lait macules (HP:0001042); Ras signaling pathway (WP:WP44) —LEADS_TO→ Neurocutaneous melanosis (HP:0012727); NF1 (HGNC:7770) —DISRUPTS→ NRAS (HGNC:7929); NRAS (HGNC:7929) —INCREASES→ Ras signaling pathway (WP:WP44). Loss-of-function mutations in NF1 lead to reduced activity of the neurofibromin protein, which normally acts as a negative regulator of the Ras signaling pathway. This dysregulation results in hyperactivation of Ras signaling, contributing to the development of cafe-au-lait macules seen in NF1. In some individuals, particularly those with more severe or mosaic mutations in NF1, this aberrant Ras signaling can also drive the proliferation of melanocytes, leading to neurocutaneous melanocytosis. Additionally, mutations in NRAS, a component of the Ras pathway, can also contribute to these phenotypes, and NF1's loss of function can indirectly lead to NRAS activation.

Loss-of-function mutations in NF1 lead to reduced activity of the neurofibromin protein, which normally acts as a negative regulator of the Ras signaling pathway. This dysregulation results in hyperactivation of Ras signaling, contributing to the development of cafe-au-lait macules seen in NF1. In some individuals, particularly those with more severe or mosaic mutations in NF1, this aberrant Ras signaling can also drive the proliferation of melanocytes, leading to neurocutaneous melanocytosis. Additionally, mutations in NRAS, a component of the Ras pathway, can also contribute to these phenotypes, and NF1's loss of function can indirectly lead to NRAS activation.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the NF1 gene and Ras signaling pathway in both conditions could lead to the development of targeted therapies, such as MEK or Ras inhibitors, that could be beneficial for both neurofibromatosis type 1 and neurocutaneous melanocytosis.
